spans.text: In the early ages of Somnus Domina, when the first Cosmic Teardrop fell, the world was invisibly bathed in its radiation. This powerful energy was undetectable to most creatures, but those who had accumulated power and age were receptive to it. Beings that were within the realm of gods and were knowledgeable about the multiverse were affected by this radiation. Cut off from their echoes and soaking up this power, beasts such as ancient dragons mutated and underwent extraordinary changes. Ancient dragons became feathered, with their bodies taking on new properties and their wings becoming massive, beautiful feathered tapestries.

Feathered dragons acted as resonators that could drag the teardrop’s radiation with them, and through their aid early mortals could harness eidomancy to cast spells, but only when in the presence of a feathered dragon and with great risk to themselves. These dragons offered aid to the Eidolons in their battle against the Grand Primaries, both as mounts and allies, apart from a few that became turncoats or fled the conflict.

When Vestias tried to establish the Eidomantic Web they were her greatest tool, and for this reason it is still said that dragons granted magic to the mortals of Somnus Domina, though the truth is more nuanced. After the Eidomantic Web was re-established, many feathered dragons offered to teach mortals magic that they had lost from the Old World, and even after they scattered and hid themselves in the world they continued to act as resonators that help to regulate the Web.

Feathered Dragons still exist, many hiding, many living in other Planes, and several being the personal assistants of the Eidolons. Metallic feathered dragons stand ready to protect the world from other threats like the Grand Primaries, while their chromatic counterparts have taken to old habits and seek to gather kingdoms, worshippers and hoards worthy of them.

Feathered dragons do not require food, water, sleep or air, are immune to the effects of extreme temperature (though not damage from energy types) and volatile environments. They do not age, and their location cannot be discerned magically without their permission.

“A dragon made of gemstone sounds beautiful. In our world, where crystals so often infer divinity, it’s hard not to imagine them as divine in nature. I hope one day to get to touch a gemstone feather so I can grasp what such a material must feel like.”

“The divine often presents itself in crystal form, with higher levels of deity displaying this more prominently. In spite of this, eidolos (not divine) and feathered dragons (not divine) are more ‘crystalline’ in nature than even the highest-ranked gods. So maybe thinking of divinity as spawning the aesthetic is putting the cart before the horse. Perhaps it’s true that eidomantic radiation causes crystallization and that anything attuned to it presents this way. That would explain why eidolic deities are connected to it, but why do feathered dragons and eidolos - mutated by and made of the stuff respectively - display it more obviously? In that sense, the crystal comes before the divine.”

“If feathered dragons ‘spread’ magic worldwide by evenly distributing eidomantic radiation, what would happen if they disappeared? Or if they hadn’t helped us to begin with? We’re fortunate for their presence.”

“I’ve noticed that dragons taking humanoid forms favor humans and elves as their guises. I wonder why that comes to them so naturally. Personally, if I intended to hide in humanoid form, I’d become a capy’hado!”
